- Surfaces: .lp-glass (with ::before specular line and the @supports fallback), .lp-frost, .lp-inset, .lp-code, .lp-hairline-grid, .lp-hairline-cell, .lp-notice-pill
- Bento: .lp-bento with [data-area] spans
- Demo frame: .lp-demo (with ::before light pool and [data-inview] rule), .lp-demo-head, .lp-demo-title, .lp-demo-lead, .lp-demo-body, .lp-demo-status, .lp-demo-foot, .lp-demo-actions
- Controls: .lp-button-lg, .lp-sheen, .lp-chip, .lp-select, .lp-seg, .lp-seg-legend, .lp-seg-legend-hidden, .lp-seg-options, .lp-seg-input, .lp-seg-pill, .lp-seg-full, .lp-link
- Status: .lp-dot and its colour modifiers, .lp-pulse, .lp-bar, .lp-bar-fill with data-run fill, drain, full and empty, .lp-scan-host
- Reveal and hover: .lp-reveal, .lp-anim-rise, .lp-anim-slide, .lp-anim-fade, .lp-anim-tick, .lp-lift, .lp-spot, .lp-bezel
- Ambient pause: rules under .lp[data-ambient='paused']

Keyframes, all inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference): lp-rise, lp-fade, lp-slide, lp-tick, lp-pulse, lp-fill, lp-drain, lp-scan, lp-sheen, lp-drift-1, lp-drift-2, lp-drift-3.

Reduced-motion delay-zeroing block.

Rules: no hex anywhere. Borders only var(--line), rgba(210, 221, 238, a) or transparent. Radii only tokens.

export function useReducedMotion(): boolean

- Built on useSyncExternalStore over matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').
- Returns true when window or matchMedia is missing. The server snapshot is also true.

export function useReveal<T extends HTMLElement>(): React.RefCallback<T>
export function revealStyle(index: number): React.CSSProperties  // returns { '--i': String(index) }

- One module-level shared IntersectionObserver: threshold 0, rootMargin '0px 0px -12% 0px'.
- On intersect it sets node.dataset.inview = 'true' and unobserves the node.
- Without IntersectionObserver it sets the attribute immediately.
- The ref callback is stable and returns a cleanup.

export type SequenceStep = { at: number; run: () => void }
export type Sequence = { play: (steps: ReadonlyArray<SequenceStep>) => void; cancel: () => void }
export function useSequence(): Sequence

- play and cancel keep stable identities.
- play cancels pending timers first.
- When reduced motion is on (via useReducedMotion), play runs every step synchronously, sorted by at.
- Otherwise it schedules one setTimeout per step, including at: 0.
- Timers are cleared on cancel and on unmount.

export function useCountUp(target: number, active: boolean, durationMs?: number): number

- Default duration 600ms.
- Reduced: returns target.
- Motion on, before the first activation: returns 0.
- On the first activation: rAF ease-out cubic from 0 to target.
- On a later target change while active: animates from the displayed value to the new target over 300ms.
- setState only in rAF callbacks.
- Callers render the value aria-hidden, with a visually-hidden final value beside it.

export function usePointerSpot<T extends HTMLElement>(): React.RefCallback<T>

- Active only when matchMedia('(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)') matches and motion is not reduced.
- pointermove writes --mx and --my in px, relative to the element, coalesced with rAF.
- Returns a cleanup.

export type LandingMotion = { reduced: boolean; ambientPaused: boolean; setAmbientPaused: (paused: boolean) => void }
export function LandingRoot({ children }: { children: ReactNode }): ReactElement
export function useLandingMotion(): LandingMotion

LandingRoot:
- Renders div.lp with data-motion='on' or 'off' and data-ambient='running' or 'paused'.
- Inside it: div.lp-aurora (aria-hidden) with three span.lp-aurora-blob, then children.
- Provides the motion context.

useLandingMotion:
- Calls useContext and useReducedMotion unconditionally.
- Outside a root it returns { reduced, ambientPaused: false, setAmbientPaused: no-op }.

export function LandingSection(props: { id: string; labelledBy: string; children: ReactNode; className?: string; tight?: boolean }): ReactElement
- Renders section.lp-section, adding lp-section-tight when tight, with aria-labelledby and tabIndex -1, wrapping div.lp-shell.

export function SectionHead(props: { eyebrow: string; title: ReactNode; titleId: string; lead?: ReactNode; aside?: ReactNode; band?: boolean }): ReactElement
- A Reveal with .lp-head.
- .lp-head-main holds <Eyebrow> and h2.lp-h2 (plus .lp-h2-band when band is set).
- .lp-head-aside holds the lead as .lp-lead, then the aside. It renders only when either is present.

export function Reveal(props: { as?: 'div' | 'article' | 'li' | 'figure' | 'aside' | 'header' | 'section'; index?: number; className?: string; id?: string; labelledBy?: string; children: ReactNode }): ReactElement
- Adds lp-reveal, the useReveal ref and revealStyle(index ?? 0).
- Uses conditional spreads for optional attributes.

export type DemoArea = 'approval' | 'failover' | 'audit' | 'cited'
export type DemoFrameProps = { area: DemoArea; index: '01' | '02' | '03' | '04'; name: string; title: string; lead: ReactNode; status: string; children: ReactNode; footnote?: string; busy?: boolean }
export function DemoFrame(props: DemoFrameProps): ReactElement

Renders article#{area}, with:
- data-area and class 'lp-demo lp-frost lp-spot lp-reveal';
- revealStyle with index 0, 1, 2 or 3 by area;
- aria-labelledby '{area}-title';
- a ref that merges useReveal and usePointerSpot.

Children of the article, in order:
- header.lp-demo-head: <Eyebrow>{index} · {name}</Eyebrow> and Tag neutral 'Simulated'
- h3#{area}-title.lp-demo-title
- p.lp-demo-lead
- div.lp-demo-body with aria-busy when busy
- p.lp-demo-status with role status and aria-atomic
- the optional p.lp-demo-foot

export type IconName = 'check' | 'dash' | 'x' | 'lock' | 'pause' | 'play' | 'arrow-right' | 'link' | 'link-broken' | 'document' | 'route' | 'gate' | 'clock' | 'slash' | 'pencil' | 'reset'
export function Icon(props: { name: IconName; size?: 14 | 16 | 18; className?: string }): ReactElement

- Inline SVG: viewBox 0 0 16 16, stroke currentColor, strokeWidth 1.6, fill none, aria-hidden, focusable false.
- Default size 14.
- No Unicode glyphs.

Types:
export type AgentCategory = 'operations' | 'engineering' | 'growth' | 'support'
export type AgentId = 'hr' | 'eng' | 'research' | 'support'

AGENTS: 4 entries of { id, name, category, title, detail }. The copy is verbatim from the current Landing.tsx USE_CASES.

Constants:
- PROVIDERS: 7 names
- SANDBOX_MODEL
- TOOL_SERVERS: 6 names
- SERVICE_COUNT = 8
- PERMISSION_CODE_COUNT = 46
- BUILT_IN_ROLE_COUNT = 5
- SIMULATED_PAGE_NOTICE
- CTA
- DEMO_ACCOUNTS_HEDGE

All exact strings are in spec 4.8.

Vitest and Testing Library. Four tests:
- useReducedMotion is true without matchMedia.
- useSequence runs steps synchronously when reduced.
- DemoFrame renders an empty role=status element and the 'Simulated' tag.
- SegmentedControl calls onChange on click.

No hex, and no '!' in JSX text.

Classes:
- Bar: .lp-bar-sentinel, .lp-bar, .lp-bar[data-solid='true'] .lp-bar-inner, .lp-bar-inner, .lp-bar-nav, .lp-bar-actions, .lp-bar-cta[data-visible], and .lp .nav-pill[aria-current='location']
- Hero: .lp-hero, .lp-hero-grid, .lp-hero-copy (load stagger via lp-hero-enter), .lp-hero-title, .lp-hero-accent (with the @supports fallback), .lp-hero-lead, .lp-hero-ctas, .lp-hero-caption
- Fact strip: .lp-facts, .lp-fact, .lp-fact-value, .lp-fact-label
- Console: .lp-console, .lp-console-stage, .lp-console-depth (parallax translate from --px and --py; no rotation), .lp-console-layer, .lp-console-back, .lp-console-trace, .lp-console-approval, .lp-console-pool, .lp-console-chrome, .lp-console-stats, .lp-console-table, .lp-console-verb, .lp-console-caption
- Pause: .lp-hero-pause

Also: container queries at 520px, the breakpoints in spec 6, and the keyframe lp-hero-enter.

Rules: borders and radii follow R3 and R4; no hex.

export function LandingBar(): ReactElement

Renders:
- div.lp-bar-sentinel
- header.lp-bar[data-solid], containing:
  - Brand
  - nav.nav-capsule.lp-bar-nav, aria-label 'On this page', with 4 nav-pill anchors (Agents, Demos, Roles, Limits) wired to useInPageLink and aria-current='location'
  - a.button.button-outline 'Sign in'
  - a.button.button-primary.lp-bar-cta 'Try a demo account' with data-visible

Three IntersectionObservers (sentinel, #lp-hero-ctas, scrollspy with rootMargin '-45% 0px -50% 0px'). No scroll listeners.

The spec is in 6.1.

export function Hero(): ReactElement

Renders section.lp-hero (aria-labelledby 'hero-title') containing .lp-shell.lp-hero-grid.

Copy column, in order:
- <Eyebrow>
- h1#hero-title with span.lp-hero-accent
- the lead
- div#lp-hero-ctas with two lp-button-lg anchors (the primary has lp-sheen and the arrow-right Icon)
- the caption with a green dot
- ul.lp-facts.lp-glass with 4 anchor cells using useInPageLink

Then <HeroConsole />. Exact copy is in spec 6.2.

export function HeroConsole(): ReactElement

Figure structure:
- figure.lp-console with span.lp-bezel and .lp-console-stage
- three .lp-console-depth wrappers holding the back, trace and approval layers (the approval layer is inert until it arrives)
- light pools
- the visible figcaption and a visually-hidden summary

Driver:
- setInterval of 250ms, gated by motion, ambientPaused, useInView (threshold 0.3, once false) and document.hidden.
- The frame comes from heroFrame(elapsed).

Also:
- The pause button (aria-pressed, constant label 'Pause motion') calls setAmbientPaused.
- usePointerParallax.

Reduced motion: a static frame at COMPOSED_ELAPSED_MS and no button.

No DataTable: use plain table.table markup. The spec is in 6.3.

Exports:
- CYCLE_MS = 10000
- COMPOSED_ELAPSED_MS = 5000
- the types HeroRow, HeroTraceLine and HeroFrame
- heroFrame(elapsedMs: number): HeroFrame

heroFrame is pure and implements the exact formulas in spec 6.3 (stats, rows, trace and arrival). It imports AgentCategory from shared/landingFacts.

export function usePointerParallax(enabled: boolean): { hostRef: React.RefCallback<HTMLElement>; stageRef: React.RefCallback<HTMLElement> }

- pointermove is normalised to -1..1 and lerped at 0.1 per rAF frame.
- The loop stops when the change is below 0.001; pointerleave returns the values to 0.
- Writes --px and --py on the stage.
- Inactive unless enabled. It cleans up its listeners and rAF.

Classes:
- Controls and stage: .lp-run-controls, .lp-run-stage (container split at 640px)
- Timeline: .lp-run-timeline, .lp-run-step[data-state] (every state from spec 7.3), .lp-run-step::before (connector as a background), .lp-run-marker
- Card: .lp-run-card-slot, .lp-run-placeholder (1px dashed var(--line)), .lp-approval, .lp-approval-meta, .lp-approval-actions, .lp-approval-note
- Payload: .lp-run-payload, .lp-run-json-key, .lp-run-json-str, .lp-run-json-punc

Layout rules for 375px. Optional keyframes use the lp-run- prefix.

Rules: borders var(--line) or the glass rgba only; radii from tokens; no hex.

State:

- autoplay per spec 4.9

- canDecide
- initApprovalState(reduced)
- approvalReducer

- STEP_COPY

export function PayloadView(props: { payload: Readonly<Record<string, string>>; label: string }): ReactElement

- The JSON is pretty-printed from the object, with spans .lp-run-json-key, .lp-run-json-str and .lp-run-json-punc.

Failover classes:
- .lp-route-presets, .lp-route-config, .lp-route-chain
- .lp-route-node[data-state] (background tints from spec 8.1)
- .lp-route-index, .lp-route-name, .lp-route-packet (transform from --lp-hop; hidden at container width 520px and below)

Cited-answer classes:

Also 375px rules. Keyframes use the lp-route- or lp-cite- prefix.

Rules: R2 to R5 apply.

export function FailoverDemo(): ReactElement

Builds on: DemoFrame (area failover, index 02), preset chips, a fieldset holding the chain rows with native selects and visually-hidden labels, SegmentedControl for policy, Send and Reset buttons, the trace ol (not live), the packet, and the outcome Tag.

Playback: planRoute events played through useSequence. Breaker memory, autoplay of the throttled preset, and the reduced initial state as specified.

The spec is in 8.1.

Exports:
- ProviderId, CHAIN, SkipFault, CallFault, Fault, Policy, Config, PresetId, PRESETS, NodeState, TraceLine, Outcome, RouteEvent
- FAULT_LABEL, SKIP_REASON
- planRoute(config, policy): RouteEvent[]
- summarise(outcome): string
- applyEvents(state, events) for synchronous folding

Exact timings and copy are in spec 8.1.

Tests, one per case:
- throttled: Groq answers with 1 failover.
- bad_key: Gemini answers, and a breaker event is emitted for OpenRouter.
- provider_down: Anthropic answers.
- safety_refusal: the chain stops and later nodes are not tried.
- everything_down: failed_closed or degraded, depending on policy.
- The event at values are non-decreasing.

export function CitedAnswerDemo(): ReactElement

Builds on: DemoFrame (area cited, index 04, busy while answering), question chips, Clear, user and agent bubbles, citation marker buttons (aria-controls, aria-pressed, hover and focus preview), and the sources aside with 8 page thumbnails (.lp-scan-host), the retrieval line and the passages li#cite-passage-1 and li#cite-passage-2.

Playback: useSequence drives the word reveal at 22ms per word. Autoplay asks 'send'. The reduced initial state is answered.

The spec is in 8.2.

- QuestionId, QUESTIONS, Segment
- ANSWER (segments)

- DECLINE
- DOCUMENT_NAME = 'Project_Proposal.pdf'

export function AgentsSection(): ReactElement

- Renders LandingSection#agents (tight) with SectionHead, then .lp-agents-grid of 4 Reveal articles (.lp-agents-tile lp-frost lp-lift lp-spot).
- Each tile has a category Tag, an h3, the detail, a tool-chip group (aria-pressed, roving tabindex) and a polite grant sentence with a lock Icon when gated.
- Data comes from AGENTS and agentGrants. The spec is in 9.1.

export const AGENT_GRANTS: Record<AgentId, ReadonlyArray<{ server: (typeof TOOL_SERVERS)[number]; sentence: string; gated: boolean }>>

- Holds the exact sentences in spec 9.1, verified against DemoAgentSeeder.
- The first gated entry is the default.

Exports:
- fnv1a32(input): 8 lowercase hex characters
- AuditEntry, Recorded
- GENESIS = '00000000'
- ENTRIES (4 entries, seq 1041 to 1044, copy in spec 9.2)
- record(entries), tamper(entries), verify(recorded, current)

No '#' characters anywhere.

export function LimitsAndCta(): ReactElement

Renders LandingSection#limits as a 7 | 5 split.

Left panel (.lp-limits lp-frost): <Eyebrow>, h2#limits-title, and a hairline ol of the four verbatim limits with mono index and slash Icon.

Right panel (section.lp-cta.lp-glass, aria-labelledby cta-title): .lp-aurora-low, <Eyebrow>, h2#cta-title, copy, two lp-button-lg anchors (the primary with lp-sheen), and the hedge caption.

The spec is in 9.5.

export function LandingFooter(): ReactElement

- footer.lp-footer containing .lp-shell.lp-footer-row.
- The caption 'AI Workforce OS, an enterprise multi-agent platform.'
- nav-pill links 'Sign in' (/sign-in) and 'Create a workspace' (/create-workspace).

export function Landing(): ReactElement

- Imports '../styles/landing/index.css' once.
- Composition exactly as in spec section 3: LandingRoot, skip link, LandingBar, main#main.lp-main, Hero, AgentsSection, the demos LandingSection with an inline head containing a literal <Eyebrow>Try it here</Eyebrow>, and .lp-bento holding ApprovalDemo, FailoverDemo, AuditChainDemo and CitedAnswerDemo; then RoleSwitcher, PlatformBand, LimitsAndCta and LandingFooter.
- Keeps a short header comment on honesty.
- No hex, and no '!'.

One change only, in the title effect: when !signedIn && path === '/', use the '/home' title pattern, so the signed-out root reads 'A governed AI workforce · AI Workforce OS'.

Change nothing else.

Delete the unused .landing-bar and .landing-grid rules, and the .landing-bar rule inside the 900px media query.

Change nothing else. The test slices for .card, .navbar and .input must stay byte-identical.
